title: The big-chopped stranger who outplayed the carnival band
summary: A shabby young cornetist with huge lips came to sit in, and amazed the classically trained band by playing anything without music.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I'm -- I guess even now, a stranger comesin, he wants a job, he wants to sit in, or join the band. The guys try to make it -- some guys want to make it tough for them, you know. Say who is this guy? So well, we'll lay something on him and see what he knows, see what he can do. And they make it hard then they chase you out and they'll have a big laugh.

This big guy, a big young guy -- you see he was young. He had a big gut on him, and big heavy thing, and his socks, his heels were out, and he came in and he wanted -- he had -- I'll never forget. He had chops that looked like two doughnuts. Man, I never saw a kid with such big chops in all my life. And I say yes? He say I'm looking for a job. I say what do you play? He had a cornet -- wrapped up in a newspaper in a bag there. He said I play this. You play that? The guy looked at it and just started laughing as if to say this guy will never get those lips in a mouthpiece. No.

So they said, okay. So they finished doing what they were doing, (practicing,) and so they say -- took stick out some music. But they always -- on those carnivals and places they always had a trunk full of music, and most of those guys, they were classical players. I mean they were musicians. They didn't worry about playing jazz, and they called that hokum. Said you play that. You play that. That's not for us.
I see. You were the only hokum player there?

Yeah I was. That's what they were -- [preferred to do] (inaudible). You know? So this guy, they pulled out the music, and he say -- he say I don't need that. He brought his hand down and started to play, and then he zzzzz, rrr, rrr,rrr, played [fast] and took and looked over at another page another guy's playing. He stopped at that point. He played -- he found out he could play any of the instruments, and doggone well. He was a heck of a musician.
I was thinking about that the other day. I was trying to think of his name. By golly, I don't know, because --
Did anything ever become of him?
Not there. Not there. I don't know what became of him. He disappeared just like he did to me, and he was gone. And what a man.
